question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y={5}^{4x+3}$ at the point where $x=-1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={5}^{u},\,u=4x+3.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={5}^{u}\ln(5),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=4.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={5}^{u}\ln(5)\cdot (4) \\ & =(4)\cdot {5}^{u}\ln(5) \\ & =4\cdot {5}^{4x+3}\ln(5).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=-1} & =(4)\cdot {5}^{4(-1)+3}\ln(5) \\ & =4\cdot {5}^{-1}\ln(5) \\ & =\frac{4 \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=-1$ is $\frac{4 \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5}.$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x=-1$ is

$$
y_1={5}^{-1}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(\frac{1}{5})&=(\frac{4 \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5})\left(x-(-1)\right) \\ y&=\frac{4 x \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5} + \frac{1}{5} + \frac{4 \ln{\left(5 \right)}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y={4}^{-6x-1}$ at the point where $x=0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={4}^{u},\,u=-6x-1.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={4}^{u}\ln(4),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-6.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={4}^{u}\ln(4)\cdot (-6) \\ & =(-6)\cdot {4}^{u}\ln(4) \\ & =-6\cdot {4}^{-6x-1}\ln(4).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=0$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=0} & =(-6)\cdot {4}^{-6(0)-1}\ln(4) \\ & =-6\cdot {4}^{-1}\ln(4) \\ & =- \frac{3 \ln{\left(4 \right)}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=0$ is $- \frac{3 \ln{\left(4 \right)}}{2}.$

Also, the $y$-value of the point on the curve where $x=0$ is

$$
y_1={4}^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Finally, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1&=m(x-x_1) \\ y-(\frac{1}{4})&=(- \frac{3 \ln{\left(4 \right)}}{2})\left(x-(0)\right) \\ y&=- 3 x \ln{\left(2 \right)} + \frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
